insSteps: Peel and roughly chop the onion. Do the same with the fresh herbs.
Drain the chickpeas carefully and dry them well in a clean kitchen towel. This step is important to avoid a dough that's too wet.

In the bowl of a food processor, add the chickpeas, onion, herbs, garlic, spices, salt, and pepper. Process until you get a grainy texture, somewhere between a thick purée and couscous. Don't aim for a smooth texture.

Pour the mixture into a mixing bowl. Add the olive oil, baking powder and flour, then stir. If needed, add one to two tablespoons of water to get a dough that holds together. It should be pliable but not sticky.
Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour. This resting time allows the dough to firm up: it will be easier to shape and the falafels will hold together better when cooked.
Using your hands, form balls the size of a walnut. Press them down slightly, without compacting them too much, then place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and drizzle with olive oil.
Preheat the oven at 190 °C. Bake for 20 minutes or until golden and crispy.
